topic: DAA - Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock (Single and Infinite Transactions)

questions.questionText: What is the core greedy idea for obtaining the maximum profit with a single buy‑sell transaction?
options: Buy at the highest price and sell at the lowest price
Buy at any price and sell at any later price
Buy and sell on the same day
Buy at the lowest price and sell at the highest price after it
questions.correctAnswer: Buy at the lowest price and sell at the highest price after it
questions.explanation: The greedy strategy is to buy when the stock price is at its minimum seen so far and sell later at the maximum price, ensuring the largest possible profit for a single transaction.

questions.questionText: After processing the fourth day's price (value 7) in the sequence 3, 9, 1, 7, 2, 20, what are the current minimum price and the maximum profit recorded so far?
questions.explanation: Day 1 sets min=3, profit=0. Day 2 updates profit to 6 (9-3). Day 3 lowers min to 1, profit stays 6. Day 4 price 7 gives profit 7-1=6, which does not exceed current max profit, so max profit remains 6 and min stays 1. Hence after day 4 the min price is 1 and the max profit is 6.

questions.questionText: How is profit calculated differently in the greedy solution when multiple buy/sell transactions are allowed compared to the single‑transaction greedy solution?
options: The multiple‑transaction approach sums the profit of every upward price movement, while the single‑transaction approach takes only the maximum difference between a low price and a later high price
The multiple‑transaction approach takes only the maximum single price difference, whereas the single‑transaction approach adds up all positive day‑to‑day differences
Both approaches compute profit in the same way, but the multiple‑transaction version repeats the calculation for each day
The multiple‑transaction profit is always exactly twice the profit of the single‑transaction solution
questions.correctAnswer: The multiple‑transaction approach sums the profit of every upward price movement, while the single‑transaction approach takes only the maximum difference between a low price and a later high price
questions.explanation: With multiple transactions you can capture profit from every rise in price (e.g., sum of (7‑3)+(9‑1)+(20‑1)=31), whereas a single transaction can only capture the best overall rise (e.g., buy at 1 and sell at 20 for profit 19).
